entries.name: com.apple.lskdd
entries.note: Reopened from n/a (audit 2026-10-17): purpose unknown. entries.name: com.apple.screensharing
entries.bifrost: springboard/src/shell/sharing_page.rs, springboard/src/privd/screen_sharing.rs, springboard/src/privd/accounts.rs, packaging/arch/bifrost-wayvnc.service, packaging/arch/pam-bifrost-wayvnc, springboard/rfb, springboard/apps/remote
entries.note: Settings > Sharing > Screen Sharing switches bifrost-wayvnc.service (privd service.set). Wired 2026-10-17: the switch first asks for the account that may sign in (screen_sharing.configure), privd makes a per-computer RSA key and writes the wayvnc configuration (enable_auth and enable_pam on, RSA-AES key, bound to the local-network address, never an open or unauthenticated port), and the unit is off until turned on. The Screen Sharing viewer and the RFB protocol crate (springboard/rfb) exist, and the Remote app runs wayvnc on a private socket.
entries.ready_note: Screen Sharing is real end to end on the host side: privd/screen_sharing.rs builds the configuration (authentication and PAM on, RSA-AES key from ssh-keygen, address from `ip -4 addr` skipping container and tunnel interfaces), privd refuses to start the unit without an account, a key and a local-network address, the PAM service limits sign-in to the one account (pam_listfile), and the Settings switch opens the account prompt first. Unverified until a Midget run: that wayvnc accepts enable_pam with rsa_private_key_file and uses the PAM service name wayvnc, and that a viewer on the LAN signs in. A system unit, not a user unit: BifrOSt has no systemd user manager. The bind address is chosen when the switch is turned on, not followed when DHCP changes it.

It serves the IOKit SCSI Architecture Model family; on Linux the SCSI midlayer (sd, sg) and udev do this in the kernel, so BifrOSt has nothing to add in user space.
